subject: BlueNova trial — scaling & capacity playbook / next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Nguyen <elaine.nguyen@bluenova.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BlueNova trial — follow-up & capacity summary

Hi Elaine — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed playbook for the trial so we can align on success criteria and the capacity plan.

Summary of discovery (short):
- Primary use case: on-device control loop + autonomous navigation assistant used by field robots; inference calls sent from BlueNova edge orchestrator to Redwood Private/VPC.
- Expected steady-state traffic for POC: ~150 requests per minute (concurrency ~10–12), average prompt length ~400 tokens, response target ~300 tokens.
- Peak bursts during tests: up to ~400 rpm (~25–30 concurrent requests) for short windows (1–3 minutes) during fleet-wide scenario runs.

Proposed POC capacity (initial):
- Reserved: 4 x A100 equivalent GPUs (reserved capacity for the dedicated POC window).
- Autoscaling policy: allow burst to 8 GPUs for sustained queueing >90s or CPU/RAM-based queue depth threshold; max burst window 10 minutes unless extended by ops.
- Concurrency target: 12 concurrent steady, with headroom to 28 concurrent during bursts using cache-aware batching.

Performance & success criteria (to validate during trial):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation < 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), < 800ms for full 300-token responses in worst-case scenarios.
- Reliability: >= 99.5% successful responses (no error/timeout) across test harness runs.
- Quality: pass automated eval set (we'll run your 500-pair prompt set) with >= 92% task accuracy and <2% hallucination rate on key intent extraction.
- Cost envelope: target average per-1k-token cost < $X (we'll finalize after model selection/quantization).

Operational items / who owns what:
- Redwood (Sergio): deliver initial runtime config, batching policy, and baseline latency/cost estimates by Apr 7.
- BlueNova (Elaine/Tom): provide eval prompt set + representative traffic replay (50–100k tokens) by Apr 8.
- Laura: coordinate internal billing/contract and confirm reserved capacity dates.
- Rishi: run kickoff and act as primary trial PM.

Attachments: I attached a short MOU and a capacity estimate workbook that outlines sample GPU-hours and expected token costs.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Apr 7: Redwood delivers config and final capacity number for reservation.
- Apr 9–16: Data ingest, replay runs, and baseline performance runs.
- Apr 17–21: Validation against success criteria and refinement (can extend if needed).

Let me know if the latency/cost targets look off from your expectations or if we should swap to a lighter quantized model for lower cost. Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BlueNova trial — runtime config suggestion

Rishi / Laura — adding technical suggestions for the POC runtime and autoscaling.

Suggested runtime config (initial):
- Model family: start with a 13B open-weights baseline (FP16), offer an 8-bit quantized variant for run cost tests.
- Serving nodes: each A100-style GPU can handle ~3–4 concurrent full-length streams (300 tokens) with our optimized kernels; with 4 GPUs targeted you get ~12–16 steady concurrency.
- KV cache warmup: use prefix caching for repeated control prompts (saves ~20% compute for repeated telemetry).

Autoscaling & burst handling:
- Warm standby: recommend 1 standby node (pre-warmed VM with runtime loaded) to reduce attach time to ~20–30s.
- Cold attach: 90–120s typical depending on region.
- Scaling rule: scale +1 GPU per sustained queue depth > 8 for 45s; scale down after 3m of underutilization.

Test harness notes:
- We will run three ramp tests: 1) steady 12 concurrent for 30m, 2) ramp to 28 concurrent for 3m, 3) repeated short bursts (10s every minute) to simulate flaky network conditions.
- Sergio will own the test runs and will post logs to the shared Drive folder.

I'll drop a quick config snippet and resource estimate in the Drive link.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
